question: Can a full-field cache plus independent three-layer execution remove duplicate Thomas generation, retain exact RGB16 bytes, and bring the 12MP Android raw core inside the provisional 8-second boundary?

mechanism.field_cache: three full-resolution float32 uncentered Thomas fields
mechanism.parallelism: three independent colour layers; per-layer row and Neumaier order unchanged
mechanism.development: each layer develops in place after all exact raw means are frozen
mechanism.output: original row-major interleave, neutral gauge and sRGB16 quantization order

fixture.profile: exact P8CN synthetic amplitude, fields, neutral gauge and exposure formula

development_observation: A nontracked 12MP prototype produced the exact legacy RGB16 SHA on host and Android. Host sequential caching reduced wall time from 6.45-6.92s to 4.86-4.92s. Android sequential caching reduced 13.61-14.45s to 11.02-11.19s; independent field generation reduced it to 9.95-10.01s; independent field plus development execution reduced it to 7.28-7.33s. No profile, dimensions, partition, output order or arithmetic threshold changed.
claim_ceiling: Private exact 12MP raw RGB16 core performance on Windows x64 and Android 14 x86_64 virtual device; not PNG/file publication, physical arm64, JNI/app/media integration, calibrated film response or complete product export performance.
